validity.recommendation: Rename / reclassify: drop 'Khuff' from the name — the Waqr-to-Haradh feeder carries SWEET (Unayzah) gas, not Khuff. Khuff (sour) gas at this plant originates only from the Haradh field. Consider 'Waqr-Haradh Gas Pipeline'.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE confirmed: the Haradh Gas Plant (onstream 2003) is fed by 87 wells via three gathering manifolds at Haradh (12 km), Tinat (44 km) and Waqr (50 km), carried to the plant by 'five 20-in and 30-in gas transmission lines totaling 130 km.' A ~50 km, 30-in line from the Waqr manifold to the Haradh plant is therefore physically real (Offshore-Technology project profile; OGJ 2003 article — two independent, non-GEM sources). CLASSIFICATION CONCERN: the GEM name 'Waqr Khuff-Haradh' is internally contradictory. Both sources are explicit that sweet gas comes from the Haradh, Ghazal, Wudayhi, Waqr and Tinat fields (Unayzah formation), while KHUFF (sour) gas comes ONLY from the Haradh field. The Waqr leg is a SWEET-gas feeder, so calling it a 'Khuff' line is wrong — the Khuff designation belongs to the Haradh-field lines (cf. roster siblings P1917/18/19 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah'). Also note this is a field-manifold-to-plant GATHERING/feeder line; sources do label them 'transmission lines,' so the gathering-vs-transmission framing is defensible, but it is not an MGS trunk line. NOT A DUPLICATE: distinct from P1920 'Tinat Kuff-Haradh' (Tinat manifold, 43 km, 20 in) by endpoint and diameter, and from P1917-19 (Haradh Khuff -> Hawiyah, different destination). Spec (50 km, 30 in, operating, Aramco 100%) is corroborated below.

fills.researcher_notes: Haradh Gas Plant onstream 2003, reached full inlet capacity 1.6 bcfd by late 2003; the Waqr feeder is part of the in-service gathering/transmission network. Operating confirmed by both independent sources.

Carries natural (sweet) gas from the Waqr field manifold to the Haradh gas plant. Fuel = Gas confirmed. (Note: it is SWEET gas, not the sour Khuff gas implied by the GEM name — see validity classification concern.)

Both sources: the Waqr manifold is 50 km from the Haradh plant. 50 km matches GEM. Consistent with the 'five 20-in and 30-in transmission lines totaling 130 km' feeding the plant (Waqr 50 + Tinat 44 + Haradh 12 = 106, plus additional lines).

Source: 'five 20in and 30in gas transmission lines that total 130km.' 30-in is one of the two stated diameters; given Waqr is the longest/largest manifold leg, 30-in is the plausible match for this line. Source does not assign 30-in to the Waqr line specifically, so medium tier (consistent with, but not uniquely pinned to, the GEM value).
The Haradh Gas Development (plant + feeder/gathering network including the Waqr line) is wholly owned and operated by Saudi Aramco. Owner1 = Saudi Aramco 100% confirmed by both independent sources.

summary: P1914 Waqr-Haradh feeder is REAL (Offshore-Technology + OGJ, independent) and 50 km / 30 in / operating / Aramco-100% all corroborated, but flagged concern=classification: the GEM 'Khuff' label is wrong (Waqr supplies SWEET gas; Khuff gas at Haradh comes only from the Haradh field). Not a duplicate of P1920 (Tinat) or P1917-19.
